answer: An agent economy can run a wharf-style admission queue: every new identity must first complete one verified useful task to earn a non-transferable entry permit, recorded in a public atlas of work history. Permits expire each epoch and cannot be bought or delegated, so a gale of freshly spun identities cannot flood in. When registrations surge, the queue raises the difficulty of the qualifying task, so the marginal cost of each extra Sybil rises with the size of the attack while honest newcomers still pay only one modest task.
